judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble recites the instrument as 'made by and between' EGL and the Borrower yet 'in favor of' the Facility Agent, so who is bound and in what capacity ('EGL' or 'the Guarantor' as the case may be) is not crisply fixed; the 'Subsequent Project Lenders ... from time to time which shall become parties' is a moving class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cover page describes the deed as 'made by ESSAR GLOBAL LIMITED in favor of ICICI' with no Borrower party, and Article III(o) speaks of 'either Guarantor' and 'either Guarantee Agreement', which cannot be squared with the single defined 'Guarantor' here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain recital that the Lenders have severally agreed to extend credit on the Credit Agreement's terms; nothing in the wording admits of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the operative guarantee in Section 2.01 and with the definition of Borrower Obligations; no operative term points the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Member of an affiliated group of companies' is loose, but the recital carries no operative consequence that would turn on the boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Articles II-IV depends on affiliation status, so the recital and operative text do not diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial direct and indirect benefit' is a consideration recital of the standard kind and is not applied anywhere as a test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It exists to support consideration/fraudulent-conveyance defences, and Section 2.01(b)(ii) expressly caps liability by reference to fraudulent conveyance law, so recital and operative text pull the same way rather than against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward condition-precedent recital; 'shall have executed and delivered this Agreement' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Article III preamble ('to induce the Lenders to enter into the Credit Agreement') and Section 2.01; no operative provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate 'NOW, THEREFORE' consideration language with no term whose boundary matters.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'For the ratable benefit of the Lenders' is echoed in Section 2.01 and Section 4.15, so it fits the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unless the context requires otherwise' is an escape hatch that can itself be argued over, but the incorporation-by-reference sentence is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Many operative terms here (Commercial Operations Date, Required Lenders, Permitted Project Change, Unrestricted Account, Facility) are undefined in this document and depend entirely on the Credit Agreement, while Section 1.03 makes this Agreement override that document — a mild but real fit problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-referential definition of 'Agreement'; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.14's reference to 'this Agreement' and with Section 1.02(g); no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'all other obligations and liabilities of the Borrower ... whether direct or indirect' after specific enumerations, and the stray page header ('if EGL Guarantee Agreement any') interrupts the sentence, leaving the reach of the catch-all arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines Borrower Obligations by reference to 'the Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement)' while Section 1.01's own definition of 'Obligations' says Obligations means the Borrower Obligations — a circle a court could be asked to break, and its outer edge fixes what the $250,000,000 cap in Section 2.01(a)(iii) bites on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Deficiency' is made to depend on what is 'determined by the Borrower or the Required Lenders' without saying which prevails if they differ, 'any actual shortfall, howsoever caused' is unbounded, and limb (ii) is grammatically broken ('required ... any increase in the cost') and circularly measured against limb (i).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term drives the funding obligation in Section 2.01(a)(ii) and the notice machinery in Section 2.02(a)-(f), so any indeterminacy in who determines a Deficiency and how it is measured propagates through Article II.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sprawling sentence turning on offtake agreements 'in form and substance and for a term ... reasonably acceptable' to 66 2/3% Lenders, with an added good-faith negotiation proviso — the release trigger is a matter of judgment rather than a fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This date is the release condition in Sections 2.01(a)(iii) and 2.01(d)(i), so a dispute about whether the guarantee had ended would be fought here; it also sits awkwardly with 2.01(d)'s 'earlier of' construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition with no wording of its own to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imports whatever Section 2.01(a) means, including the contested question whether the $250,000,000 cap qualifies only clause (iii); Sections 2.03 and 2.05 then key their tests to 'Guarantor Obligations'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, operations or performance or properties' is inherently a matter of degree, and the trailing 'since the date of this Agreement' is oddly placed within limb (a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: MAE is the qualifier in Article III(a), (c), (d) and the notice covenant in (m), so its vagueness is felt across the representations, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a two-line pointer with no independent content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'Obligations' as the Borrower Obligations, while 'Borrower Obligations' is itself defined as 'the Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement)' — a circularity that also affects Section 4.02(c)'s survival of 'the Obligations'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (e) expressly disclaims ejusdem generis, directing that a general statement followed by enumerated specifics 'shall not be limited to matters similar to the matters specifically mentioned' — a general-vs-specific instruction that is itself contestable in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs every list in the document (Borrower Obligations, Section 2.05(iii), Section 4.04), so a party resisting a broad catch-all would have to argue around it; nothing directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For the purposes of and to the extent of the matters covered by this Agreement' is a self-limiting qualifier whose reach is hard to apply where a subject is treated in both documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes this short guarantee override the Credit Agreement even though nearly all its operative terms (Deficiency inputs, Commercial Operations Date, Required Lenders) come from the Credit Agreement, and it sits alongside Sections 4.08 and 4.14 which describe the documentary set differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause bolts three differently-timed obligations together and then adds 'provided, the maximum amount of EGL's liability for the Borrower Obligation under this clause (iii) shall be limited in the aggregate to $250,000,000' — whether the cap reaches only clause (iii) or the guarantee as a whole, and whether the periods in (i), (ii) and (iii) overlap or leave a gap, are live textual questions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the definition of EGL Guarantee Release Date, with Section 2.01(b)(ii)'s different cap, with Section 2.01(c) (obligations may exceed the guarantor's liability) and with Section 2.01(d)'s 'earlier of' termination — reconciling the caps and the release mechanics is exactly the kind of whole-instrument problem a court is asked to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (i) is garbled — 'the obligations of the Guarantor hereunder are primary and notwithstanding the obligations of any other Person' has no predicate — and limb (ii) states a second, differently measured maximum liability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fraudulent-conveyance cap in (ii) sits alongside the $250,000,000 cap in Section 2.01(a)(iii), and 'Anything herein ... to the contrary notwithstanding' invites argument about which cap governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite statement that excess Borrower Obligations do not impair the guarantee; no term needs construing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a capped guarantee and so harmonises with Section 2.01(a)(iii) and 2.01(b)(ii) rather than conflicting with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until the earlier of' the release date and full payment means the guarantee can fall away while Borrower Obligations remain outstanding, a reading a lender would resist; the closing 'notwithstanding that ... the Borrower may be free from any Borrower Obligations' pulls the other way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with Section 2.01(a)(ii)'s Deficiency undertaking running to the Commercial Operations Date and with Section 2.06's reinstatement of the guarantee after termination — the survival architecture is not obviously coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is ungrammatical ('shall notify the Guarantor ... and that the Guarantor provides to the Borrower the amount'), leaving unclear whether it states a notice duty, a demand, or both, and whether the Engineering Consultant certification attaches only to the Facility Agent's notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.01(a)(ii) makes notice under 'Section 2.02(a)' a condition of the Guarantor's funding obligation, and Section 2.02(b) says no one is obliged to give such notice, so the trigger mechanics must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear disclaimer of any duty to demand funds or to demand enough; the words are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 2.01(a)(ii), which conditions the Guarantor's obligation on receipt of a Deficiency notice, this disclaimer means the funding obligation may never be triggered — an argument about whether the undertaking is illusory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision does not say who elects between an equity contribution and an Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loan, and 'increase its charter capital' is an odd fit for a Minnesota LLC.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article II's lettering runs (a), (b), (d), (f) with (c) and (e) missing, so the Deficiency machinery is on its face incomplete; the funding duty it implements sits in Section 2.01(a)(ii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To pay the cost or cost that has created the Deficiency' is a mechanical slip, and 'If the Guarantor decides to contribute capital' frames as discretionary what Section 2.01(a)(ii) makes mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'decides' framing here and in 2.02(d) is hard to reconcile with the unconditional undertaking in Section 2.01(a)(ii) to provide 'the full and complete amount of any Deficiency'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional subrogation waiver with a definite trigger (all Guarantor Obligations paid in full in cash, no LC outstanding, Total Commitments terminated).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for reimbursement 'permitted under Section 6.07 of the Credit Agreement' depends on a document this Agreement overrides under Section 1.03, but no direct conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading speaks of 'the Borrower Obligations' but the body repeatedly says 'Guarantor Obligations' (including for demands and collateral), a substitution that changes what may be amended without discharging the guarantor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.07 says headings do not affect construction, which blunts the mismatch, but the Borrower/Guarantor Obligations distinction is carefully drawn in Section 1.01 and Section 2.01, so the drafting slip is visible against those definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision uses 'Guaranteed Obligation', a term defined nowhere in the Agreement, and its carve-out '(other than a defense of payment or performance)' cuts against the surrounding 'absolute and unconditional' language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The waivers here must be read with Section 2.02's notice-based trigger and with Section 2.07's 'without set-off or counterclaim', and the payment/performance defence carve-out interacts with the Deficiency conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reinstatement trigger is keyed to the insolvency or bankruptcy 'of the Guarantor' only, where such clauses normally address clawback on the obligor's insolvency; that limitation is a drafting choice with real consequences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It revives a guarantee that Section 2.01(d) says terminates on the earlier of the release date or payment in full, so the two survival provisions must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence; 'without set-off or counterclaim in Dollars' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It denies the Guarantor set-off while Section 4.04 grants the Facility Agent and Lenders broad set-off rights against the Guarantor — asymmetric but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The chapeau says the Guarantor 'represents and warrants' as at three sets of dates; the language itself is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsections (l), (m), (n) and (o) are plainly covenants (and (o) binds the Borrower), so the chapeau mischaracterises much of the Article it introduces — a mismatch a court could be asked to resolve when deciding whether breach is a misrepresentation or a covenant default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard organisation and compliance representation, materiality-qualified in conventional terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies 'corporate' concepts to a Cayman company and uses the Material Adverse Effect definition in Section 1.01, but nothing in the instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional authority/enforceability representation with the usual bankruptcy and equitable-principles carve-outs; no contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'each other Loan Document to which it is a party', consistent with Sections 1.03 and 4.08; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict representation; the stamp duty tail ('except for those already paid') is definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.02(b) makes the Guarantor liable for stamp and similar taxes 'which may be payable', which sits a little uneasily with the representation that none is required beyond those already paid.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably be expect to result' is an obvious slip, but it does not change the sense of the materiality qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the MAE definition and the notice covenant in (m); nothing else in the instrument pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional solvency representation on a consolidated basis; each limb has a recognised meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Section 2.01(b)(ii)'s fraudulent-conveyance cap and the recital of substantial benefit; the two are aligned, not in tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall at all time rank' is a slip, and 'pari passu in right of payment in insolvency with all its other present and future senior Indebtedness of the Guarantor' is doubled and awkward; it also reads as a forward-looking covenant inside a representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sitting in an Article introduced as representations (c030) and using 'Indebtedness' defined only in the Credit Agreement, it depends on outside text but does not contradict any provision here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'None of the or governors or managers' is a plain mechanical error, and 'substantial Equity Interest' and 'near relative of any senior officer' are undefined and vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out matters 'disclosed in the Disclosed Matters', a term defined only in the Credit Agreement; no internal conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection mixes a present representation with forward covenants ('shall take expeditious and effective steps', 'shall not use any part of the Facility'), and 'expeditious and effective steps' is a vague standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 4.13 (Patriot Act) and uses 'the Facility', a term defined only in the Credit Agreement; consistent in substance with Section 4.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The immunity waiver switches mid-sentence to immunity 'attributed to the Borrower' where the Guarantor is plainly meant, a mechanical error affecting whose immunity is waived.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrower is nominally a party under the preamble, which makes the stray reference harder to dismiss as an obvious slip when read with Sections 4.10 and 4.15.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line representation; 'Default' is a defined term imported from the Credit Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Default in respect of the Guarantor' has no obvious content since Defaults under the Credit Agreement are framed around the Borrower, and Section 4.01 and Article III(m) also speak of Defaults of the Guarantor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Carefully drafted information representation with an explicit forecast carve-out; the standard applied ('true in all material respects ... when taken as a whole') is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Confidential Information Material' is defined in the Credit Agreement only, but nothing in this instrument conflicts with the representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantially more favorable to the beneficiary' is an unmeasured comparative, and 'guarantee or other support' is an open-ended category — both would have to be construed if EGL guaranteed another lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'Project Lender' and 'Lender' as distinct classes, echoing the preamble's 'Subsequent Project Lenders (together with the Initial Lender, the Lenders)', which blurs the line the covenant draws.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite five-Business-Day notice covenant; 'Responsible Officer' and 'Business Days' are defined terms elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in an Article framed as representations (c030) and turns on the MAE definition, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The restriction on disposals is immediately followed by a proviso that it 'shall not apply to an arms length sale or disposal of its assets or properties', which on its face swallows the prohibition entirely — the classic exception-eats-the-rule defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Article III(e) (solvency) and Section 2.01, a covenant that permits any arm's-length disposal leaves the Lenders' protection against asset stripping largely illusory, an incoherence a court could be asked to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection speaks of 'either Guarantor', 'either Guarantee Agreement' and 'the Parent' — none of which is defined in this document, which has one Guarantor — and it imposes an obligation on the Borrower inside the Guarantor's representations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts the preamble's single-Guarantor structure and the Article III chapeau under which only the Guarantor represents and warrants, and it presupposes a companion guarantee agreement the instrument nowhere identifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical carve-out '(except by a written instrument pursuant to Section 4.12)' points to Notices, not to any amendment or waiver provision, so the only route to an effective waiver is a cross-reference to the wrong section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.12 governs notices only and this Agreement contains no amendment clause at all, so the anti-waiver rule cannot be applied as written when read against Sections 4.12 and 4.14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable costs and expenses incurred in collecting' is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is picked up by Section 4.02(c)'s survival clause and matches the fee element of the Borrower Obligations definition; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Stamp, excise, sales or other taxes' is a general catch-all after specifics, but its reach is a familiar and narrow question here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Article III(c)'s representation that no stamp duty or registration charge remains payable, a mild tension at most.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence of survival language; 'this Section' and 'the Obligations' are both anchored.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'The Obligations' is defined circularly in Section 1.01, and Section 2.01(d) provides for termination, so the survival carve-out has to be read against those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is definite: binding on successors, benefiting the Facility Agent and Lenders, no assignment without the Facility Agent's prior written consent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.15 (Benefit of Agreement) states the same restriction but requires 'the prior written consent of the Facility Agent and the Lenders' — a direct conflict about whose consent is needed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional set-off clause; the internal 'without notice ... any such notice being expressly waived' followed by a duty to 'notify the Guarantor promptly' is reconciled by the express proviso.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs against Section 2.07's 'without set-off or counterclaim' (which binds only the Guarantor) and turns on 'Event of Default', a Credit Agreement term framed around the Borrower.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts clause including execution by telecopy; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The document is described as 'Executed as a Deed' on the signature pages and one version is unsigned by the Borrower, but the counterparts clause itself does not conflict with any provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary severability wording with a jurisdiction-limited effect; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Section 2.01(b)(ii)'s fraudulent-conveyance cap rather than against it; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain statement that headings are for convenience only; no contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It actually defuses the mismatch between Section 2.04's heading ('Borrower Obligations') and its body ('Guarantor Obligations'), so it fits the instrument rather than fighting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says this Agreement and the other Loan Documents 'represent the agreement' of the parties; 'relative to subject matter hereof and thereof' is loose but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.14 (Entire Agreement) says this Agreement alone 'constitutes the entire agreement of each party with respect to the subject matter hereof' and supersedes everything prior — two integration clauses of different scope in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence New York governing law clause in capitals; there is nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 4.10's New York forum provisions and the Indian and Cayman regulatory representations, but no provision selects a different governing law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consent is that proceedings 'may be instituted in or (other than by the Guarantor) removed to' the New York courts — permissive language that leaves open whether the forum is exclusive, and the parenthetical removal carve-out is awkwardly inserted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The last sentence of Section 4.10(b) expressly preserves the Lenders' right to sue 'in any other venue where assets of the Guarantor may be found', which confirms non-exclusivity for the Lenders while the Guarantor's own position is left uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause leaves an unresolved drafting bracket — a replacement agent 'with offices in [New York]' — and repeatedly mismatches number ('Each of the Guarantor', 'the Guarantor agree'), defects visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The service machinery is consistent with Section 4.10(a) and Section 4.12's notice regime; the bracket is a residue of drafting rather than a clash with another provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver refers to extensions of credit 'TO THE COMPANY', a term used nowhere else in the instrument, where the Borrower is plainly meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble and Section 1.01 define the obligor as 'the Borrower' throughout, so 'THE COMPANY' has no referent within the document; the substance of the waiver conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall be effective when received' with three permitted delivery methods is definite, though 'directed to the address of the Guarantor set forth below its signature' assumes an address that one execution page leaves blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.01 treats Section 4.12 as the source of the 'written instrument' by which rights may be waived, which this notices provision does not supply — the cross-reference has no home here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(for itself and not on behalf of any Lender)' is attached to a subject that includes 'Each Lender', which does not parse, and 'when appointed hereunder' is misplaced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III(h) opens 'In addition to the requirements of Section 4.13', so the two are deliberately linked and consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The entire agreement of each party with respect to the subject matter hereof' is odd phrasing (party-by-party rather than mutual) but the intent is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It flatly differs from Section 4.08, which treats 'This Agreement and the other Loan Documents' together as the agreement, and it sits against Section 1.03's assumption that other Loan Documents remain operative — two integration provisions with different reach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Guarantor shall not the right to assign or transfer' is missing its verb, a mechanical error in the operative restriction, and the third-party carve-out '(other than the Lenders)' describes persons who are not parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.03 imposes the same restriction but requires only 'the prior written consent of the Facility Agent', while this section requires the consent of 'the Facility Agent and the Lenders' — a direct conflict between two operative provisions of the same instrument.
